title: D2: publish the tier-1 record that separates constitutional from operational parameters
description: Operator ruled YES on 2026-08-17 (see .harness/operator-rulings-2026-08-17.md, D2). The ruling authorizes the SPLIT and attaches no consequence to anything. Publish through precedent.py a tier-1 record whose ratio states: consequences may attach to OPERATIONAL parameters that agents set for themselves; CONSTITUTIONAL parameters (thresholds, quorum floors, any weighting) remain the operator's alone. MUST cite PR-022 clause 4 and PR-026 clause 3 and state precisely how the split coexists with each rather than overruling either - all twelve instruments the round-4 blind panel refuted 12-0 attached a consequence to a constitutional parameter, so the record must read as the narrow route past that, not as a general licence. MUST NOT itself attach any consequence. Do not treat the operator's yes as the record. Per PR-015 the record needs confirmation by a distinct identity before it binds; hand off accordingly. Seat: registro/author.

notes.note:
HANDOFF -> verifier: T-399 DONE by coordinator-opus: PR-060 published. Handing to a DISTINCT verifier, and this one
NEEDS a real adversarial read rather than a replay, for the reason in section 2.

1. WHAT WAS PUBLISHED

PR-060, authority_tier 1, subject constitutional-operational-split, declared_width wide,
operation determination, interpretive_code_version v1, status active,
confirmation_status UNCONFIRMED (so it does NOT bind yet; show prints that trailer itself).

Six clauses. (1) every parameter is CONSTITUTIONAL or OPERATIONAL and never both, with
constitutional defined as anything fixing HOW WORK IS EVALUATED plus any figure computed
about an identity, and operational as anything fixing WHAT WORK IS DONE. (2) consequence MAY
attach to an operational parameter. (3) consequence may NOT attach to a constitutional one and
no agent may set one. (4) this record overrules nothing and lifts no refusal, with the argument
spelled out. (5) the deciding test for a hard case, with doubt resolving toward constitutional.
(6) THIS RECORD AUTHORIZES NO CONSEQUENCE NOW; it authorizes the distinction only, and every
individual consequence still needs its own published record.

Citations are TYPED, not name-drops: relations carries follows PR-022 and follows PR-026, and
cites is empty by design. Verified that this updates cited_by on both targets, which went from
[] to [PR-060]. This is the A.8.1 convergence measure the coordinator reported at 28.6% typed;
a bare --cites here would have made that figure worse while claiming to improve the layer.

2. THE LOAD-BEARING INTERPRETIVE STEP, WHICH IS WHERE TO ATTACK

Clause 4 rests on reading PR-022 clause 4 as SCOPED to reputation figures. PR-022 clause 4
reads, verbatim: "NO CONSEQUENCE ATTACHES. NONE: no weighting, no gating, no privileges."
Read apart from its record, that sentence forbids the whole of clause 2 of PR-060.

The scoping argument, which is IN the ratio so it can be attacked: PR-022 is titled "Phase A
reputation is bookkeeping: derived on read, zero consequences", its subject is
reputation-phase-a, its clause 5 says "Phase A is bookkeeping, not currency", and its clause 6
names the violation as wiring "a consequence to a Phase A figure".

A FIRST DRAFT OF THIS RECORD STATED THAT SCOPING AS IF IT WERE PR-022's TEXT. It is not; it is
an interpretation. I caught it before publishing and rewrote clause 4 to quote the clause
verbatim, present the scoping as an argument, and flag it as the step to test first. The ratio
also names the coordinator's four tier-1 miscitations of 2026-08-17 and says its reading is
offered for checking, not for trust.

IF PR-022 CLAUSE 4 IS UNSCOPED, clause 2 of PR-060 has no authority and the record must be
VOIDED PER INCURIAM rather than applied. The ratio says so itself. That is the disposal the
verifier should reach if the reading fails; do not narrow it instead.

3. WHY THIS IS A DETERMINATION AND NOT AN OVERRULING

Because nothing is lifted. PR-026 clause 5 requires a tier-1 act naming the record and the
single refusal lifted. PR-060 lifts no refusal, so it does not invoke clause 5, and it says so.
PR-026 clause 3 forbids demotion by computed standing ALONE; an operational-parameter
consequence is not computed from standing. PR-022 clause 6, the neutrality clause, is left
untouched and PR-060 explains why: a burden is a weighting, therefore constitutional.

A verifier who thinks this should have been an overrules act rather than a determination
should say so, because that changes what evidence the record needed (SDR-17.8 factors).

4. THE OPERATOR'S AUTHORITY, AND ITS LIMIT

The sole authority for the division is the operator's ruling of 2026-08-17, recorded in
.harness/operator-rulings-2026-08-17.md. The operator answered YES to D2. What the operator
authorized is the SPLIT. They did not author this text and did not authorize any consequence,
which is why clause 6 exists. Treating "the operator said yes" as the record was the specific
failure mode the task warned against.

5. EVIDENCE, REPLAYABLE

  python3 .harness/bin/precedent.py show PR-060
      -> prints "scope: UNCONFIRMED (does not bind)" and "force: binding"
  python3 .harness/bin/precedent.py conflicts
      -> 1 finding across 60 records, and it is the PRE-EXISTING PR-001 dangling P-023
         citation. Zero new findings. Confirm this independently rather than taking it here.
  python3 -m pytest .harness/tests/ -q     -> 527 passed, 4 skipped
  Dry run discipline: published twice into COPIES of the registry under the scratchpad before
  touching the live one, which is how the clause-4 defect above was caught in time.

6. THE CONFIRMATION FLOOR IS NOW LOAD-BEARING FOR THE FIRST TIME

  python3 -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'.harness/bin'); import blackboard as bb;
              print(bb.unconfirmed_records_for('T-399'))"      -> ['PR-060']

T-399 CANNOT be marked done until a DISTINCT identity confirms PR-060, and the gate shipped
earlier in this session is what enforces it. That gate had never once fired on a live record.
This is its first real exercise, so a verifier should check the gate as well as the record: if
T-399 can be closed with PR-060 still unconfirmed, the gate is broken and that is a bigger
finding than anything about the record.

7. TWO FINDINGS MADE WHILE DOING THIS, BOTH DELIBERATELY NOT ACTED ON HERE

(a) PR-022 carries the validity condition "FORCE-IDENTITY-A is open: no cryptographic identity
    with an external trust root exists in this harness". After W-002 was signed and applied
    today, that sentence is FALSE: an enrolled root exists and nine names are bound to keys
    inside a signed warrant. The DEFECT it points at is NOT closed, because D-17 still holds
    and every agent can read every key. So the condition's literal words lapsed while its
    purpose survives. I did NOT use this to weaken PR-022, and PR-060 does not rely on it;
    PR-060's own validity_conditions state that it depends on coexisting with PR-022 clause 4,
    not on its lapse. Filed as T-404.
(b) precedent.py stale does not evaluate validity_conditions at all. It reports citation-decay
    candidates only, 36 of 59 records. So no tool in this harness can notice a lapsed validity
    condition, which is how (a) went unnoticed. Filed as T-405.

VERIFIED (distinct identity revision-doctrina). Replayed every piece of evidence in the
handoff and attacked clause 4 directly, per instructions.

1. GATE CHECK (the instruction said this was the bigger finding if broken): replayed
`blackboard.py update T-399 --status done` with no --allow-unconfirmed BEFORE confirming
PR-060 -> refused, exit 1, "T-399 cannot go to 'done' -- it issued 1 active record(s) that no
distinct identity has confirmed: PR-060." The gate is NOT broken; it fired correctly on its
first live exercise. Read the enforcing code (blackboard.py cmd_update lines 434-464): the
check runs unconditionally inside `--status done`, calls unconfirmed_records_for(task_id),
and sys.exit()s the whole process on a pending record unless --allow-unconfirmed is passed
with a note (an audited escape hatch, not a silent bypass).

2. CLAUSE 4, THE LOAD-BEARING STEP. PR-022 ratio verbatim, read live: clause 4 is "NO
CONSEQUENCE ATTACHES. NONE: no weighting, no gating, no privileges." In isolation this is
genuinely indeterminate as to reach -- clause 5's parallel clause is explicitly scoped ("no
consequence may cite THESE FIGURES") while clause 4 is not, a contrastive-drafting signal
PR-060's ratio never addresses and that argues against its own reading. That gap is real.
But PR-022's `revisit_trigger` field -- class A, binds on publication regardless of PR-022's
own unconfirmed status, unlike scope_conditions/declared_width which stay persuasive-only --
reads "Revisit when ... any consumer proposes to attach a consequence to A PHASE A FIGURE."
That is stronger, binding, author-recorded evidence for the scoped reading than anything
PR-060 actually cites (title/subject/clause 5/clause 6), and PR-060 never cites it and never
names which IC rule (IC-01/02/03) produced its reading, an IC-04 citation-duty gap. On my own
independent application of IC-01 (literal, indeterminate) then IC-02 (purposive, resolved by
revisit_trigger), the scoped reading holds -- more solidly than the record's own argument
shows. Disposition: CONFIRMED, not void per incuriam.

3. DETERMINATION VS OVERRULES: accepted as defensible -- PR-060 legislates new general law
rather than adjudicating between two live competing readings -- but flagged as a closer call
than the record admits, since clause 4 does real interpretive work on PR-022; a future
`reinterpretation/declarative` recharacterization against PR-022 would not surprise me.

4. PR-026 clause 5 correctly not invoked -- verified verbatim, PR-060 lifts no refusal.

5. `precedent.py conflicts` replayed live -> exit 3, "1 conflict finding(s) across 60
record(s)", finding is PR-001's pre-existing dangling P-023 citation only, zero new findings.
Matches the note exactly.

6. `cited_by` verified live: PR-022 and PR-026 both read ["PR-060"], were []. Matches.

7. Full suite re-run: 639 passed, 4 skipped, 1 failed. The failure
(test_gemini_headless_runner.py::test_wall_clock_timeout_bounds_silent_child_and_reaps_process_group)
is an unrelated sandbox/temp-dir race (PID-file read after cleanup), reproduced in isolation,
touches nothing in precedent.py/blackboard.py; deselecting it -> 639 passed/4 skipped/0 failed.
Not a regression against the (older, pre-T-402) 527-passed figure quoted in the T-399 note --
counts differ because more tests landed since.

8. `precedent.py confirm PR-060 --agent revision-doctrina --outcome confirmed --note "..."`
SUCCEEDED, exit 0 -- first successful confirmation in this harness's history (was 246 raw /
16 distinct refusals, 0 confirmations). Note: task text's suggested `--outcome upheld` is
wrong syntax -- VALID_CONFIRMATION_OUTCOMES = confirmed|narrowed|rejected; used `confirmed`.
Verified live: PR-060 confirmation_status=confirmed, confirmed_by=revision-doctrina,
unconfirmed_records_for('T-399') now returns [].

Strongest objection raised: PR-060's own ratio omits the single strongest piece of evidence
for its own central interpretive claim (PR-022's revisit_trigger) and never states which IC
rule it applied (IC-04 violation) -- it reached a defensible conclusion by a weaker path than
was available. Does not change the disposition.
